result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make the same sound per-candidate decisions, keep cues for events that happen while the customer isn't looking, and cover toggles, OS silent/DND settings and visible fallbacks. A is tighter and makes a couple of sharper calls: it sends 'heading out' only after 'I'm here', and it marks only that alert as time-sensitive. A also comes closer to the testing point by asking to check that the ready chime fires reliably. Neither answer clearly says that vibration and sound support varies by device and browser, or that it needs testing on real devices, and B is longer than a team thread needs despite good extras like avoiding double alerts. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both give clear per-candidate decisions, favor alerts that reach someone who isn't looking, and cover toggles, silent mode/DND and pairing every cue with something visible. B edges ahead with practical details: it fires the haptic only after the server confirms, sends 'heading out' only after 'I'm here', and tells the team to check that the chime fires reliably. That last point comes closest to admitting device support varies, though neither answer says outright to test on real devices. B overstates when it calls sound 'the only way to reach them', and A's data plan for settling the disagreement is a nice touch, but B is slightly more actionable overall.
